beats.say: Three bad days are coming.
A region goes dark. A bad update wipes the prices. And a partner feed shows up late.
beats.label: What will go wrong

beats.say: Design the platform so each one is a non-event.
beats.label: Station 5.5 · Failure mitigation
beats.head: Make each one a non-event

check.prompt: One message crashes the pipeline every time. Where does it go?
options: Back to the front of the queue
check.why: A dead-letter queue takes the bad message aside. The pipeline continues.

beats.say: First: assume everything fails sometimes.
When a call fails, retry. But wait longer each time, with a little randomness.
beats.label: Retry the right way
beats.head: Backoff, with jitter

beats.say: If everyone retries every second, they knock the service down again.
beats.label: Exam trap
beats.text: Retrying every second until it is back

beats.say: Make writes safe to repeat, so a retry never doubles the data.
beats.label: Idempotent writes
beats.head: A retry must not double the data

beats.say: Save your place with checkpoints. Then a restart picks up where it stopped.
beats.label: Checkpoints
beats.head: Save your place

beats.say: And send poison messages to a dead-letter queue. The pipeline keeps going.
beats.label: Dead letters
beats.head: Poison messages go aside

beats.say: Second: a whole location fails.
A zone is one building. A region is a city with several buildings.
beats.label: Zone or region
beats.head: Zone: a building. Region: a city.

beats.say: Most managed services are regional. They survive one zone failing, on their own.
beats.label: Zone failure
beats.head: Regional services survive a zone

beats.say: A whole region failing needs two things from you.
beats.label: Region failure
beats.head: A region needs two things

beats.say: Data that is copied to another region. And a way to start the compute again over there.
beats.label: For a region outage

check.prompt: A bad UPDATE ran 10 minutes ago in BigQuery. What is the fastest fix?
options: Restore the backup from last night
Rebuild the table from raw files
check.why: Time travel reads the table as it was at any moment in the last 7 days.

beats.say: Third: someone runs a bad update.
Do not reach for last night's backup yet. BigQuery has time travel.
beats.label: First choice
beats.head: BigQuery time travel

beats.say: You can read any table as it was, up to 7 days ago.
beats.sub: of time travel, to undo a mistake

beats.say: Other undo buttons: table snapshots, object versioning in Cloud Storage, and seek in Pub/Sub.
beats.label: More undo buttons

beats.say: And always keep the raw data unchanged. Then you can rebuild everything.
beats.label: The master undo
beats.head: Keep raw data. Rebuild anything.

beats.say: For the late partner feed: wait for the data with a sensor, check the row count, then backfill.
beats.label: Late or missing data
beats.head: Sense. Check. Backfill.

beats.say: Cloud SQL high availability fails over by itself. A cross-region replica needs you to promote it.
beats.label: Failover
beats.head: HA: automatic. Replica: promote it.

beats.say: And test your failover before the bad day. Not during it.
beats.label: Last rule
beats.head: Test failover before you need it

beats.say: Recap. The last one of the course.
Retry with backoff. Write idempotently. Replicate across regions.
beats.label: Station 5.5 · 1 of 2

beats.say: Keep an undo button, like time travel. And test your failover.
beats.label: Station 5.5 · 2 of 2

beats.say: That was the last station. Finish the checkpoint, then face the boss.
beats.sub: Finish the checkpoint, then face the boss.
